newsitem.title: USA: Globalstar debt offering may hit $500 mln.
newsitem.headline: Globalstar debt offering may hit $500 mln.

text.p: Globalstar L.P. is expected to increase its planned debt offering to as much as $500 million before it formally prices on Thursday or Friday, said Bill Adams, fixed-income analyst at Conseco Capital Management Inc.
The issue was planned as a 144A private placement offering of $250 million of senior notes due 2004 and warrants to buy common stock in Globalstar Telecommunications Ltd.
The company is likely to increase the value of the warrants accompanying the notes from one percent to 1-3/4 percent of Globalstar equity, Adams said.
Lead manager Lehman Brothers had no comment on the deal.

The increase in size comes about six months after market conditions forced the company to postpone the deal, analysts said. In that time, underlying market fundamentals have improved to the point where Globalstar can garner a rate in the talked-about 11-1/2 percent range.

"It's a different market," Adams said. "Globalstar, Orion Network Systems and IRIDIUM all got pulled at the same time when the stock market and the bond market was getting hit, making it a tough time to bring a new issue."
Les Levi, media and telecom analyst at Merrill Lynch & Co, said the telecommunications sector has also curried more favor with investors since the deal was pulled.
"People have been very comfortable with satellite transactions," Levi said.
Adams noted investors were also "buying off" Loral Space & Communications Ltd's 34 percent ownership of Globalstar.

But one high-yield money manager who declined to be named said an 11-1/2-percent coupon fails to match the inherent risks that face Globalstar. In fact, the manager said the tight pricing was an indication that a market top was forming.
"There is so much risk involved here," the manager said. "The company is estimating they will get close to one million subscribers in the first year and I just dont see it.
"Investors are not factoring in launch risk and satellite deployment risk. I'm really amazed, but God bless them."
